newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to decide on extent of West Bank pullback.
newsitem.headline: Israel to decide on extent of West Bank pullback.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu meets his cabinet on Thursday to discuss Israeli withdrawal from more West Bank land amid Palestinian anger over the closure of four PLO offices.
Netanyahu is bound in an agreement with the PLO to hand over more West Bank land by Friday.
A decision to pull back Israeli troops from only tiny areas could spark more friction with Palestinians already fuming over Israeli action in East Jerusalem.
An aide to Netanyahu suggested the withdrawal might be delayed until Palestinian President Yasser Arafat closed the offices of four PLO institutions in East Jerusalem.
Israeli police gave the institutions until Sunday -- two days after the deadline for Israel's withdrawal -- to close their offices or be shut down.
The United States, Israel's closest ally, criticised the move.

"How much this redeployment will be...will be decided by the cabinet on Thursday. Once a decision is made, the implementation of the decision will not take more than 48 hours," Netanyahu aide David Bar-Illan said on Wednesday.

Israel has handed over seven West Bank cities and most of an eighth to Palestinian self-rule since its landmark 1993 peace deal with the PLO. It has also given its former arch-foe civil responsibilities in some 450 villages.

The agreements, negotiated under the more dovish Labour-led government which Netanyahu ousted last year, aimed to expand Palestinian self-rule gradually as Israel and the PLO completed their permanent peace settlement by 1999.
The Jewish state retained exclusive control of some 70 percent of the West Bank, but agreed to withdraw its forces from rural areas in three stages to specific military locations.

The right-wing Netanyahu, who had opposed handing over any land to the PLO, agreed in his own deal with Arafat in January to honour the three withdrawal stages but said the scope of each would be Israel's decision alone.
Several members of his cabinet oppose any pullback.
"Israel, according to the agreements, is responsible not to enter into negotiations on this matter but to set the extent of the pullback," said Foreign Minister David Levy.
One Israeli official said that cabinet ministers were willing at most to hand over only about two percent of the rural areas still under Israeli control.
Palestinian officials said Israel had refused to discuss the extent of the first stage of redeployment and did not give them a date for the actual pullout.
Army chief Amnon Shahak flew by helicopter on Wednesday over areas in the West Bank still under Israeli occupation ahead of the cabinet meeting, security sources said.
Bar-Illan said on Wednesday that Israel wanted the Palestinian Authority to close down institutions in East Jerusalem before the redeployment takes place.
"It is impossible for the peace process to continue, for the redeployment and other obligations which Israel has, to continue without the closing of these offices," Bar-Illan told Reuters.

Israel says Arafat's Palestinian self-rule Authority is conducting political activity in these offices in violation of Israel-PLO accords. Palestinians say the offices are not affiliated with the Palestinian Authority.

Faisal al-Husseini, responsible for Jerusalem affairs in the Palestinian Authority, said the closure orders coming on the heels of Israel's plan to build 6,500 more Jewish homes in the eastern part of the city, were a deliberate provocation.
Israel claims all of Jerusalem as its eternal capital. Palestinians view East Jerusalem as the capital of their future state.
